subject.title: [Bug] Command validation bypass on multi-line tool calls in parser

question: Can security triage confirm a current-main payload where repaired multiline arguments bypass both the target tool schema and the command policy or approval boundary?
rationale: The alleged impact is security-sensitive, but the current report does not identify or demonstrate the boundary that fails, and related malformed-stream behavior has already received narrower parser hardening.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open and request a redacted payload and end-to-end validation trace through the repository's private security process before changing code.

options.title: Match prior hardening
options.body: If the payload only reproduces the earlier leading-fragment leak, document the affected release and close against the shipped parser hardening.

options.title: Confirm a distinct boundary
options.body: If schema or command-policy bypass is demonstrated, assign a narrowly scoped security fix to the owning validation layer rather than adding generic parser regexes.

recommendation.title: Request private reproduction
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and request a redacted payload and end-to-end validation trace through the repository's private security process before changing code.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent adjacent work most closely spans provider normalization and command-execution security boundaries, while the exact failing layer remains unknown.
